newsitem.title: SPAIN: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER SEEKING SPANISH HAT-TRICK.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER SEEKING SPANISH HAT-TRICK.

text.p: Double world champion Michael Schumacher is praying for more of the heavy rain which accompanied his victory in Monaco as he attempts to claim his third successive Spanish Grand Prix win this weekend.

German Schumacher, 28, whose Monte Carlo triumph put him on top of the world drivers' championship for the first time since he became a Ferrari driver at the end of 1995, believes only a wet race can keep his hopes alive.

"To be honest, I would prefer to cancel Spain because it is not a circuit which suits our car," said Schumacher. "But now that I have opened up a small gap in the championship, I suppose I can afford to just go for a points finish and still look good.
"After this race, though, I believe we will be looking reasonably good for the rest of the season. But Spain will definitely be a tough race for us. I will just have to do my best."

A downpour last year at the modern Circuit de Catalunya, set in the hills amid industrial developments inland from Barcelona, helped Schumacher score another win to add to his 1995 victory for Benetton. In a race with only six finishers, he came home just before the two-hour limit elapsed.

He recognises that another day of soaking wet weather would be to his advantage and help him maintain his narrow four-points advantage over Canadian Jacques Villeneuve, of Williams, at the head of the drivers' championship.

It would also be encouraging for his Ferrari team-mate Eddie Irvine, currently third on 14 points, and for the team, who lead the constructors' series with 38 points to Williams 30 after five of this year's 17 races.

"Nobody likes to race in the wet," said Schumacher. "But after last year and Monaco, it would probably be better as far as we are concerned if it was another wet race. But if it is dry, it is sure to be another very tactical race. Tyre wear and the number of pit stops a team has to make will play a decisive role in the outcome."

Ferrari may introduce their latest 'step 2' V10 engines in the Spanish race for the first time this year. Until now, they have been used only in qualifying and practice, but Schuamcher believes the Catalan circuit could be the right place to introduce them.
"It is an engine which is better suited to the quicker circuits so there is a good chance we will race the engine for the first time in Spain, if everything goes well in practice," he said.

Schumacher's biggest threat on a circuit used regularly by all the teams for testing is likely to come from the Williams pairing of Villeneuve and his Williams team-mate, German Heinz-Harald Frentzen.

Villeneuve finished third last year while Frentzen was fourth in a Sauber. Frentzen, winner of the recent San Marino Grand Prix and on pole position in Monaco, will be a force again in a country where he feels very at home -- he has a Spanish mother.
Without a point from the last two races, Villeneuve knows he needs a podium finish, or a victory, to maintain his place among the championship leaders and justify his pre-season status as favourite.
"All the work we've done in Barcelona during testing should be useful," he said. "I'm looking forward to racing there -- I really like all the high-speed corners."
